shell.title: Choose Language
shell.desc: Pick a language, then press start to begin the artist statement.

typingLines: Hi.
Have you been here before?
noResponseLines: Well… let me introduce the creator first.
You can call him 叶宇恒, or Frank, or whatever makes this feel more important than it actually is.
He made, is making, and might continue making games.
More like something he uploads online, and then watches dissolve quietly like a drop of water in the ocean.
If he's lucky, someone might come across one and play it.
And an even smaller chance that they'll remember it.
Let's be honest, he's just trying to entertain himself.
He's a random person making random things and hoping that they matter.
finalLines: That's it.
Are you sure you want to proceed?
finalContinueLines: All right, if you're patient enough to see this, it means you're boring as FUCK.
hiringLines: Hold on, that's getting too sentimental.
Imagine reading this as a hiring manager.

typingLines: Come on.
Don't listen to all the crap he said on the left.
I never said I was experimenting.
That was a joke, one time.
He refuses to let it go.
Other than that, he's mostly right.
If you ask me why I started making games, the answer is pretty simple, and kind of dumb.
At some point in my life, I need to figure out how I'm going to make a living.
I don't really know what I'm good at.
And I've been playing games for my whole life.
So I thought, why not try making them?
Turns out, I'm not really good at this either, just like everything else.
It took me a long time to realize that.
I don't think what I make is particularly interesting.
And I don't expect everyone to like it.
But I still want to make something that a small number of people might really care about.
It doesn't have to be fun or innovative.
If someone can look at it and think,
“oh, that's exactly what I've been feeling,”
that's enough for me.
All right, I've been talking too much.
To make this more engaging, I have some multiple choice questions for you.
He already taught you how to answer, right?
Only ONE of the following statements is FALSE.
Which one is it?
1. I'm very good at visuals.
3. There are 24 hours in a day.
response1Lines: I'm just kidding, that one was obvious.
Only ONE of the statements is FALSE.
1. I want every game I make to carry its own attitude.
2. I still haven't made anything I'm truly satisfied with.
3. I care more about whether my games are felt, rather than whether they're understood.
finalLines: So probably you get what I mean now.
This is the kind of thing I enjoy making.
Something slightly off.
Congrats, you made it to the end.
I guess that's all you really need to know about me.
My games probably say more than I ever could, so if you have time, try them.
And I genuinely appreciate any feedback.
Also, most people would call this an artist statement.
I feel weird calling myself an artist, and I definitely don't feel qualified enough to make a statement.
So I'm just trying to make this as honest as possible, and hopefully not too boring.
Thank you for reading this far.
Seriously, thank you.
Oh shit, wait…
If you're a recruiter, PLEASE ignore everything we just said.
None of it is true.
I'm extremely responsible and highly motivated.
An adaptable, proactive team player who thrives in collaborative environments.
My skills include combat design, level design, interactive system design, Unity, Unreal Engine, C#, and C++.
I'm also fluent in both Chinese and English.
I will absolutely do whatever it takes to get a job.
FOR REAL.
